Section 01

Screening Objective & Design Philosophy

This methodology describes a multi-layer screening process to identify Turkish MV distribution substations (primary substations) suitable for connecting a 9.9 MWn grid-scale Battery Energy Storage System (BESS). The 9.9 MW threshold sits just below Turkey's 10 MW regulatory boundary for simplified connection procedures under EPDK grid connection regulations.

Design Principles

Conservative-progressive funnel. Hard filters (Steps 1–9) eliminate substations that are clearly unsuitable on engineering, environmental, or geographic grounds. Soft flags (grid congestion) identify risk factors without eliminating — these inform due diligence at the site shortlisting stage. The philosophy is: eliminate what is impossible, flag what is risky, rank what remains.

Open data only. Every dataset used in this methodology is publicly available at no cost. This ensures reproducibility and independence from proprietary DSO data. Where DSO data would be superior (e.g., actual transformer ratings, real-time load measurements), we note the gap and use the best available open proxy.

Living document. This methodology is versioned and designed to grow. New filters, enrichments, and data sources will be added over time as the project progresses from screening to site shortlisting to connection application.

Regulatory context: Turkey's electricity distribution is governed by EPDK (Energy Market Regulatory Authority). Connection procedures for generation >10 MW require a full TICA process; below 10 MW, a simplified Econnextion procedure applies. Our 9.9 MWn target is deliberately sized to benefit from the simplified regime.

Section 03

Step 1 — Universe Definition

Objective

Define the universe of candidate substations: all Turkish distribution-type substations (primary substations) from OpenStreetMap, augmented with EPİAŞ (Electricity Market Operator) primary substations data.

Inclusion Rule substation.type = 'distribution' AND substation.country = 'IT' Excludes: minor_distribution (25,937 secondary substations), transmission (TEİAŞ RTN), industrial, traction, generation, converter substations.
Augmented with: 96 EPİAŞ-identified substations not present in OSM (see Section 12).

Rationale

Distribution substations are the natural connection point for MV-connected BESS. They receive HV power from TEİAŞ's transmission grid (typically 132–150 kV) and step it down to MV (10–20 kV). In Turkey, these are the primary substations, operated primarily by EDAŞ (~76%) and local distributors.

Minor distribution substations (secondary substations) are excluded because: (a) they operate at LV (400V), too low for a 9.9 MW connection; (b) their transformer capacity is typically 160–630 kVA, far below 10 MVA; (c) they have no spare HV/MV switchgear bays.

Section 04

Step 2 — Physical Space Assessment

Objective

Determine whether each substation has sufficient physical space within its fenced perimeter to accommodate the equipment needed for a BESS connection.

Connection Scenarios

Scenario A — New Transformer Bay
299 m² required
Full new HV/MV transformer bay including: power transformer (60 m²), oil containment bund (45 m²), HV circuit breaker bay (72 m²), fire wall (15 m²), MV switchgear (12 m²), cable trenches (20 m²), access road (60 m²), protection room (15 m²).
2,250 substations fit (93.6%)
Scenario B — MV Feeder Bay
23 m² required
Minimal MV connection where spare transformer capacity exists: MV circuit breaker bay (8 m²), cable trench (10 m²), protection/metering panel (5 m²).
53 additional (Scenario B only)
Space Assessment Logic available_area = fenced_area × (1 − equipment_density) pass_A  = available_area ≥ 299 m²
pass_B  = available_area ≥ 23 m²
pass    = pass_A OR pass_B

Equipment density by category: Hub 60%, Large 50%, Medium 45%, Small 35%.
Fenced area from OSM polygon footprint. Validated against Bing Maps aerial imagery at zoom 19+.

Result

OutcomeCount%
Fits Scenario A (new transformer bay)2,25093.6%
Fits Scenario B only (MV feeder)532.2%
Cannot fit either → ELIMINATED1024.2%
Section 05

Step 3 — Electrical Headroom Assessment

Objective

Estimate whether each substation has ≥10 MVA of spare firm capacity (on N-1 basis) to accommodate a 9.9 MW BESS connection without triggering overload.

Headroom Calculation headroom_MVA = firm_capacity_MVA − estimated_load_MVA firm_capacity  = (n_transformers − 1) × rating_per_tx
estimated_load = CS_count × 150 kW / (0.9 PF × 1000)
pass           = headroom_MVA ≥ 10

CS_count: secondary substations assigned via Voronoi nearest-neighbour to each CP.
150 kW per CS: ~70 households × 2.5 kW peak × 0.7 diversity factor.
N-1: loss of largest single transformer — standard EPDK planning criterion.

Data Sources

InputSourceMethod
Transformer count & ratingOSM + category-based estimatesOSM actual where mapped; EDAŞ standard assumptions by category
Downstream CS countOSM minor_distribution (25,937)Voronoi spatial assignment to nearest CP
Peak load per CSEDAŞ engineering practice150 kW (250 kVA transformer at 60% utilisation)

Result

1,924 substations pass (≥10 MVA headroom). All 439 small substations eliminated — with a single transformer, they have zero firm capacity on N-1 basis. This is the correct engineering conclusion: a 9.9 MW BESS cannot safely connect to a single-transformer substation.

Section 06

Land Radius Search — 500m Proximity Analysis

Objective

Define the candidate land search area around each substation for BESS installation. Any suitable land parcel within 500m of a substation centroid is a potential BESS site.

Buffer Generation buffer(lat, lon, r=500m) → 64-point geodesic polygon Δlat = (r × cos(θ)) / 111,320
Δlon = (r × sin(θ)) / (111,320 × cos(lat × π/180))
θ = 0, 2π/64, 4π/64, ..., 2π

WGS84 ellipsoidal approximation. 500m radius = maximum practical MV cable run
without requiring additional distribution infrastructure.

Output

ParameterValueRationale
Radius500 mMaximum practical MV cable run without additional infrastructure
Points per circle64Smooth polygon for spatial intersection accuracy
Output formatGeoJSON2,405 features, 4.1 MB
Next useIntersect with cadastral data for Step 6 land availability
Section 07

Step 4 — Generation Saturation [Informative]

Objective

Assess whether existing renewable generation already connected to a substation has consumed the available reverse-flow capacity, leaving insufficient room for an additional BESS export.

Saturation Model net_headroom_MVA = headroom_MVA − existing_generation_MW existing_gen = Σ (solar_MW + wind_MW) assigned to this CP
saturation_ratio = existing_gen / headroom_MVA
BESS_eligible = (net_headroom ≥ 10) AND (space_pass = true)

Renewable plants assigned to nearest CP by spatial proximity.
Solar default: 2 MW per plant (where OSM capacity tag missing).
Wind default: 10 MW per plant (where OSM capacity tag missing).
Only 72 of 5,653 plants have explicit OSM capacity tags.

Saturation Distribution

Saturation LevelCount%Description
No generation1,34355.8%No OSM-mapped renewable plants nearby
Low (≤30%)65227.1%Plenty of room for BESS
Moderate (30–50%)1054.4%Viable but tighter
High (50–100%)863.6%DNO may push back
Saturated (>100%)2199.1%Generation exceeds headroom

Result

1,789 substations are BESS-eligible after Step 4 (net headroom ≥10 MVA and space available). 135 eliminated due to generation saturation consuming the available headroom.

Section 08

Step 5 — Flood Zone Exclusion

Objective

Exclude substations located in high-probability flood zones that pose unacceptable risk to a 25+ year BESS asset.

Decision Rule

Flood Filter Logic IF centroid ∈ P3_polygon → EXCLUDE (floodRisk = 'high') IF centroid ∈ P2_polygon AND ∉ P3 → FLAG (floodRisk = 'moderate')
ELSE → PASS (floodRisk = 'none')

P3 (elevata): 20–50 year return period. Unacceptable for BESS.
P2 (media): 100–200 year return. Flagged for site-specific assessment.
P1 (bassa): >200 year return. Acceptable residual risk.

Data Source

SourceDatasetVintageProjectionSize
AFAD (Afet ve Acil Durum Yönetimi Başkanlığı)Turkey Flood Hazard Map (Taşkın Risk Haritası)2020TUREF / EPSG:5254P3: ~25,000 polygons; P2: ~27,000 polygons
Why AFAD mosaic as single source: The national mosaic harmonises flood hazard maps from all 7 District Basin Authorities into a consistent classification, reconciling PAI (older Law 183/89 maps) and PGRA (EU Floods Directive 2007/60/EC maps). Using a single authoritative source avoids conflicts and vintage discrepancies that arise from cross-referencing multiple regional datasets at the screening stage.

Method

GeoPandas spatial join of substation centroid points (reprojected to EPSG:3035) against P3 and P2 polygon shapefiles using R-tree spatial indexing.

Result

Section 09

Step 6 — Land Availability

Objective

Identify whether each substation has at least one suitable cadastral parcel within 500m for BESS installation. Step 6 uses a three-category classification system to capture different land assembly strategies.

Data Source

SourceDatasetVintageAccess
TKGM (Tapu ve Kadastro Genel Müdürlüğü)Parsel Sorgulama — Cadastral Parcel ServiceCurrent (live)Free / Public

Cadastral Reference — Three-Part Identifier

Each parcel returned by the cadastral service carries the complete Turkish cadastral identifier via the NATIONALCADASTRALREFERENCE attribute. The format encodes three mandatory components, ensuring full traceability to the official kadastro:

Cadastral Reference Format {İlçeCode}_{Ada}.{Parsel} İlçe — TÜİK district code (e.g., 34001 = Adalar, İstanbul)
Ada — Cadastral block number within the district (e.g., 000100)
Parsel — Individual parcel number within the block (e.g., 104)
Example ReferenceİlçeAdaParselSubstation
34001_000100.10434001 (Adalar)000100104Adalar TM
06001_006600.107706001 (Altındağ)0066001077Ankara Kuzey TM
35001_005400.5435001 (Aliağa)00540054Aliağa TM
Completeness note: The ADMINISTRATIVEUNIT field (il/ilçe code) is also stored separately, providing a cross-check. This three-part identifier is sufficient to uniquely locate any parcel in the Turkish kadastro and to request official documentation (tapu kaydı) from TKGM.

Three-Category Classification

Category A — Perfect Target
4,000–6,000 m²
Single parcel of ideal size for a 9.9 MW BESS. Requires one land acquisition, minimal legal complexity.
16,023 parcels · 1,619 subs
Category B — Land Bundle
Contiguous group ≥ 5,000 m²
Multiple adjacent parcels (each ≥500 m²) with total area ≥5,000 m² and compactness ratio ≥0.4. Requires multi-parcel acquisition.
4,899 bundles · 30 subs (B-only)
Category C — Too Large
6,000–10,000 m²
Single parcel larger than ideal but still worth pursuing. May require partial acquisition or lease of a portion.
14,683 parcels · 9 subs (C-only)
Land Availability Logic passStep6 = hasCategory_A OR hasCategory_B OR hasCategory_C Category A: single parcel with area ∈ [4,000, 6,000] m²
Category B: contiguous group of parcels (≥500 m² each, shared edges <3m gap), total ≥5,000 m², compactness ≥0.4
Category C: single parcel with area ∈ [6,000, 10,000] m²
Priority: A > B > C

Parcels queried via WFS BBOX filter (500m around substation centroid).
Area computed from GML polygon geometry using shoelace formula with latitude correction (<1% error).
Contiguity analysed via BFS on adjacency graph (vertex distance <3m threshold).

Method

For each of the 1,701 BESS-eligible substations, all cadastral parcels within 500m were retrieved from the TKGM cadastral service. Parcels between 500–10,000 m² were retained and classified. Contiguity analysis identified connected components of smaller parcels that together form viable BESS sites.

Result

Unique parcels found (500–10,000 m²)154,319
Category A parcels16,023

Category C parcels14,683
Substations passing Step 61,658 (97.5%)

Elimination pattern: The eliminated substations concentrate in mountainous eastern provinces (Eastern Anatolia) and dense urban centres where even small parcels are scarce within 500m of the substation.
Section 10

Step 7 — Terrain Slope Analysis

Objective

Filter candidate parcels by terrain slope. BESS installations require relatively flat ground (≤6% slope) to minimise grading costs and ensure safe, stable foundations for containerised battery modules.

Data Source

SourceDatasetResolutionAccess
ESA / AirbusCopernicus DEM GLO-30 (TanDEM-X derived)30m (~1 arc-second)Free / AWS S3 public bucket

Method

For each of the 59,498 candidate parcels identified in Step 6, terrain slope was computed from the Copernicus DEM using Horn's 3×3 kernel (Sobel operator) for gradient estimation. Eight directional slopes were computed along compass bearings (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) plus an omnidirectional aggregate. The best (flattest) orientation is recorded for each parcel.

Slope Computation slope_omni = √(dz/dx² + dz/dy²) × 100  [%] dz/dx, dz/dy: Horn's method (3×3 Sobel kernel) on DEM elevation grid
slope_dir(θ) = |dz/dx · sin(θ) + dz/dy · cos(θ)| × 100
pass = mean_omnidirectional_slope ≤ 6%

DEM tiles: Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF, 3600×3600 pixels, float32, EPSG:4326.
67 tiles covering Turkish parcel locations (~1.2 GB total).
Small parcels (<3 DEM pixels): centroid + 3×3 neighbourhood fallback.

Result

Pass slope (≤6%)35,799 (60.2%)
Fail slope (>6%)23,699 (39.8%)
Median slope4.4%
Mean slope9.0%
Substations passing Step 71,401 (84.5% of Step 6)
Eliminated by slope257

Section 11

Step 8 — Evacuation Route Assessment

Objective

Verify that each candidate parcel has a viable cable evacuation route to its nearest substation, routed along public roads and paths, with total distance ≤450 metres. This is the final hard elimination step.

Data Source

SourceDatasetVintageAccess
OpenStreetMapHighway ways (Overpass API)March 2026 (live)Free / ODbL

Method

Evacuation Route Logic total_distance = snap_parcel + network_path + snap_substation 1. Query Overpass API for highway ways within ~8.9 km tiles (16 highway types, excluding private access)
2. Build undirected weighted graph (NetworkX): nodes = OSM road nodes, edges = Haversine-weighted segments
3. Snap parcel centroid and substation to nearest graph nodes (max 100m snap distance)
4. Dijkstra shortest path between snap points
5. pass = total_distance ≤ 450m

~930 Overpass tiles cached for all of Turkey. Grid-cell spatial indexing (~220m cells) for fast nearest-node lookup.
If snap distance >100m for either endpoint, parcel fails (too far from road network).

Result

MetricValue
Route computations36,759
Parcels pass (≤450m route)3,312 (9.0%)
Parcels fail33,447 (91.0%)
Substations passing Step 8748 (53.4% of Step 7)
Eliminated653

Route Length Distribution (passing parcels)

MetricDistance
Minimum11 m
Median316 m
Mean297 m
P90427 m
Maximum450 m
Why 450m? The 450m threshold represents the maximum practical MV cable run for a BESS connection without requiring intermediate infrastructure (junction boxes, cable joints, or booster stations). Beyond this distance, cable losses increase, voltage drop becomes significant, and installation costs rise disproportionately. The threshold is conservative: longer runs are technically possible but economically challenging.
Section 12

Grid Congestion Flag

Objective

Flag substations located in TEİAŞ-designated critical AT areas where HV/EHV grid congestion may impede new generation connections. This is a flag only, not an elimination step — congestion is dynamic and depends on grid reinforcement plans.

Data Source

SourceDatasetVintageFormat
TEİAŞ (Turkish TSO)Kritik Bölge ve Hat Listesi (Critical Areas & Lines)1 June 2025PDF (5 pages)

TEİAŞ Critical AT Areas

Critical areas are defined per EPDK grid connection regulations as portions of the HV/EHV grid with limitations for transport of new local electricity production.

BölgeStatusSubstationsBESS-Eligible Flagged
BoluCRITICAL AT REGION5345
ÇankırıCRITICAL AT REGION9674
ErzincanCRITICAL AT REGION2417
GaziantepCRITICAL AT REGION15986
RizeCRITICAL AT REGION9174
VanCRITICAL AT REGION177145
Bursa (Balıkesir)CRITICAL PROVINCE—15
Ankara (Çankırı)CRITICAL PROVINCE—5
Congestion Flag Logic congestionFlag = 'critical_region' IF bölge ∈ {Bolu, Çankırı, Erzincan, Gaziantep, Rize, Van} congestionFlag = 'critical_province' IF (bölge, il) ∈ {(Bursa, Balıkesir), (Ankara, Çankırı)}
congestionFlag = 'none' OTHERWISE

Bölge/il assigned via offline reverse geocoding of substation centroid coordinates.
No substations are eliminated — congestion flag is advisory for due diligence.

Result

Of the 748 final candidates: 461 (27.1%) are flagged for grid congestion (441 in critical regions, 20 in critical provinces). 287 (72.9%) are in non-critical areas.

Interpretation: A congestion flag does not mean connection is impossible. A BESS in a critical area may still connect if it provides grid services (frequency regulation, congestion relief) rather than pure export. TEİAŞ's TE.R.R.A. portal (76 microzones, quarterly) and Econnextion dashboard (monthly connection queue) provide additional granularity for site-specific assessment.
Section 13

EPİAŞ primary substations Cross-Reference

Objective

Cross-reference the OSM substation dataset with EPİAŞ's official primary substations registry to: (a) assign EPİAŞ area codes (Area Code) to existing substations, enabling linkage to the regulatory framework; and (b) identify substations present in the EPİAŞ database but missing from OSM.

Data Source

SourceDatasetVintageFormatRecords
EPİAŞ (Electricity Market Operator)Interactive Map delle primary substations (2025–2027)2025ArcGIS FeatureServer (EU1)Layer 0: 2,145; Layer 5: 245

Each EPİAŞ polygon represents the service territory (Service Area) of one primary substation — not the physical substation location. After deduplication by Area Code (11-character area code), 2,143 unique areas remain, operated by 24 distribution companies (EDAŞ: 1,842 areas, 85.9%).

Cross-Reference Methodology

EPİAŞ polygon centroids (service area centres, not substation locations) were matched to OSM substations by nearest-neighbour proximity. Since centroids can be several kilometres from the actual substation, distance thresholds were analysed to find the optimal balance:

ThresholdMatch RateAssessment
3 km60.8%Too restrictive — many valid matches missed
5 km82.4%Moderate coverage
8 km92.8%Good coverage
10 km95.5%Optimal balance (selected)
15 km98.6%Diminishing returns, risk of false matches

Result

MetricValue
EPİAŞ areas matched to OSM (≤10 km)2,047 (95.5%)
OSM substations with EPİAŞ Area Code1,881 (78.2%)
New substations from EPİAŞ (unmatched)96
Match distance (median)1,520 m
Match distance (P90)2,621 m
Final Step 1 universe2,501 substations
524 unmatched OSM substations are primarily TEİAŞ/RFI transmission substations (142) not covered by EPİAŞ distribution data, plus substations in areas not included in the 2025 EPİAŞ map. These remain in the dataset with no EPİAŞ linkage.
Impact on pipeline: Steps 2–8 counts remain at 748 passing substations because the 96 new EPİAŞ subs lack Steps 2–4 data (physical space, electrical headroom, BESS eligibility). Once assessed, they will enter the pipeline and may increase the final candidate count.

Section 15

Caveats, Limitations & Assumptions

Data Quality

IssueImpactMitigation
96.7% of secondary substations lack voltage tagsCannot determine MV voltage directlyInfer from bölge (15 kV south/centre, 20 kV north)
94% of secondary substations lack operator dataCannot identify non-EDAŞ substationsAssume EDAŞ standard unless contradicted
Only 20 of 3,281 OSM transformers have rating dataCannot use actual transformer ratingsCategory-based EDAŞ standard assumptions
Only 72 of 5,653 renewable plants have capacity tagsGeneration estimates use defaults (2/10 MW)Conservative but individual plants may differ greatly
AFAD mosaic vintage is 2020May not reflect most recent PGRA updatesSite-specific due diligence at shortlisting stage
OSM road network incomplete in rural areasSome parcels may fail Step 8 due to missing roadsSite visits for borderline candidates
30m DEM resolution limits small parcel analysisParcels 500–1,000 m² may have only 1–3 pixels3×3 neighbourhood fallback for small parcels

Methodological Assumptions

AssumptionValueSensitivity
Peak load per secondary substation150 kWUrban CS may be 2–3× higher; rural CS may be lower
Equipment density (Hub/Large/Medium/Small)60% / 50% / 45% / 35%Validated against satellite imagery for one hub station
BESS connection threshold10 MVA on N-1 basis9.9 MW at ~1.0 PF; some DNOs may accept lower margin
Renewable capacity defaultsSolar 2 MW, Wind 10 MWTurkey average; individual plants vary 0.5–50+ MW
Buffer radius for land search500 mLonger cable runs technically possible but costlier
Slope threshold6%Screening-level; actual grading feasibility depends on soil and drainage
Evacuation route threshold450 mConservative; longer runs possible with higher cost
Contiguity threshold (bundles)3 m vertex distanceAccounts for coordinate precision and minor gaps
Compactness threshold (bundles)0.4 (area/bbox)Ensures roughly rectangular, usable bundle shapes

What This Methodology Does Not Cover

This screening explicitly does not address: actual transformer nameplate data (requires DSO disclosure), real-time load measurements, DNO connection queue status, detailed geotechnical or planning constraints, grid reinforcement costs, BESS commercial viability, environmental impact assessment, land-use zoning classification, or road access for heavy transport (transformer delivery). These are deferred to the site shortlisting and connection application phases.
